Subject: Post-call recap: DPA / SCC module selection & next steps

Hi Sana / Oliver —

Great to chat earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Key alignment items we discussed
- AcmeHealth confirmed the intended data flow and that Acme will act as the Data Controller for customer data. Redwood would act as a Processor for the production inference and related telemetry.
- You asked about the appropriate SCC module for the relationship (controller <-> processor).
- SOC 2 Type II and vendor security questionnaire were requested by your team.

2) Next steps / asks for your legal/security team
- Please confirm that AcmeHealth will sign Controller -> Processor SCCs (Module: Controller-to-Processor).
- Share any redlines you expect in the DPA or a link to your standard DPA.
- Upload the Vendor Security Questionnaire when convenient — I saw a couple of flags in the questionnaire that we should discuss (subprocessors, data retention, access controls).

3) Our action items
- I will send a Redwood DPA draft (based on SCC Module: Controller-to-Processor) and attach SOC 2 Type II report and a current subprocessor list.
- If helpful, we can schedule a brief legal-to-legal call next week to run through redlines.

Attachments: 20271118-acme-demo.mp4 (meeting recording)

Proposed meeting: Thu, Nov 25 10:00 AM PT — let me know if that works for you and I’ll calendar it.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Sana / Oliver —

Appreciate the confirmation. Attached are the initial artifacts from Redwood: 
- Redwood_DPA_v1.docx (DPA draft based on Controller-to-Processor SCCs)
- SOC2_2027_TypeII.pdf (redacted SOC 2 Type II report)
- Subprocessors_2027.csv (current subprocessors and locations)

Quick notes inline: 
- SCC module: We agree that Controller -> Processor is the appropriate module and have drafted the DPA accordingly. If your legal team prefers a different clause layout, we can accept redlines.
- Data retention: Redwood’s default retention for inference logs/telemetry is 30 days. We can extend/shorten based on contractual requirements — propose we add an SLA line item for retention in the DPA.
- Subprocessors: The CSV includes our current infra and cloud vendors. We have an enum with subprocessors that are used for storage, monitoring, and analytics — happy to explain any entry on a call.

Proposed next steps: 
- Legal: please take our DPA and provide any redlines (target date Dec 3 to keep timeline).
- Security: I will ask our security lead to complete the Vendor Security Questionnaire — attaching initial SOC2 now and will follow up with questionnaire answers by EOW.
- Ops: If the retention requirement changes, let me know the specific retention period you need and whether that should be scoped per-environment or per-data-type.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.docx; SOC2_2027_TypeII.pdf; Subprocessors_2027.csv

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that speeds things up.

Best,
Marissa
